text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
While passing by the train station on our
way
home, Hishi Akebono is handed a
flyer for a
planetarium. Apparently, an
expert in space
science will be
commentating on today's show.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Wow, we can learn all about stars and
space
there! And look, the flyer comes
with discount
coupons.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text: Yes, please! It sounds really fun! ♪

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
Ohhh! Hello there, Akebono! How
marvelous to
see you here! ☆

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Hi, Marvelous! What a coincidence! Are
you here
to look at the stars too?

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
But of course. ☆ I'm in search of
marvelous and
sparkly things. ★

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Oh, I hope you can find some. Hey,
looks like the
show's starting!

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
The night sky spreads out across the
domed
ceiling above us. The
commentary covers not only
the
projected constellations, but also the

composition of stars and the Milky Way.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text: There are so many stars in the universe...

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Hey, I wonder what aliens eat... Do you
think they
can eat Earth food?

text_block_list.name: Woman A
text_block_list.text:
Pfft. I can't believe there are people who
actually
believe in aliens.

text_block_list.name: Man A
text_block_list.text:
She probably thinks they're real 'cause
she
watched some sci-fi flick. How
gullible can you
get?

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Yeah... People have never seen aliens, so
it's no
wonder they don't believe in
them, huh. Oh well!

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
There are quite a few terrestrial-type
planets
throughout the Milky Way
Galaxy that could be
considered
habitable, and it's possible that some
of
them have water.

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
So it wouldn't be a stretch to say we
could find
life-forms in those
environments! Space is still full
of
mysteries, so who knows what could
happen!
How marvelous! ☆ Galactically
marvelous! ★☆

text_block_list.name: Man A
text_block_list.text: H-hey, let's get out of here...

text_block_list.name: Space Science Commentator
text_block_list.text:
Hehe. I'm pleased to see all this
enthusiasm you
have for space. If you'd
like, I could answer your
earlier
question.

text_block_list.name: Space Science Commentator
text_block_list.text: While we don't know what aliens eat... it is possible that Earth food would be edible for them.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Really?! In that case, I'd love to have
some
chanko with them!

text_block_list.name: Space Science Commentator
text_block_list.text:
Eating chanko might prove a bit difficult.
The
soup and ingredients would float all
over the
place in a zero-gravity
environment, you see.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
What?! They wouldn't just stay
together?!

text_block_list.name: Space Science Commentator
text_block_list.text:
No. That's why all space foods and
drinks are
made to be viscous. The
surface tension helps
keep everything
together.

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
How does space food taste? Is it
delicious? Is it...
marvelous?

text_block_list.name: Space Science Commentator
text_block_list.text:
You know, I think it's become quite
delicious,
actually. There are a lot of
researchers looking
into how to make
space food tastier for
astronauts.

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
Marvelous! ☆ That's just like your food,
Akebono!
Your delicious dishes make
everyone feel
marvelous too!

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
You're so right. I wonder if space food is
made by
people who want other people
to enjoy yummy
stuff too?

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
I want to learn more about space food
now!

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text: Yes! I really want to try making space chanko!
choice_data_list: 宇宙食を買って食べてみよう！

text_block_list.name: Space Science Commentator
text_block_list.text:
In that case, I think watching some
videos of
astronauts eating space food
would make for
good reference material.
They often review the
food too.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
We immediately watch some videos
during our
break. I'm grateful that
they're subtitled so we
can watch them
even in a place like this.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Whoa. So in space, water breaks apart
like that?!
This must be what that
scientist meant about the
chanko going
everywhere!

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
Ooh! When the food's canned, the
contents stay
in place even when you
turn it upside-down!
Marvelous! This
stuff looks like it'd be hard to
mix,
though.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Yeah, everything floats when there's no
gravity,
so I guess it's impossible to mix
anything...
Cooking in space sounds
really tough!

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Wow... This astronaut just said she really
likes
Japanese food, and she looks
forward to
Japanese dishes the most at
mealtimes.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
I bet she'd be over the moon if she could
try some
hot pot...

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
I'm going to try to create a recipe for
astronaut
chanko! If I make it and
upload it to Umasta,
maybe it'll inspire
space food researchers!

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
How marvelous! ☆ Let's do it! ★ We've
got to do
our best to get chanko into
space! ☆

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Yeah! Imagine if we could sit and share
chanko
with astronauts and aliens
someday!

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Oh, they're really selling it! You can buy
space
food from the souvenir corner!

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
We buy the space food versions of both
curry rice
and miso-stewed chicken to
try back on campus.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text: Okay, let's have them now!

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
The curry rice is marvelous! ☆ The spices
are
really intense. ★

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
The miso-stewed chicken tastes pretty
salty. And
they've really thickened the
soup stock.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
Apparently, space food is purposefully

over-seasoned because zero-gravity

environments dull people's sense of
taste.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
I also heard that space food is produced
with
reduced salt content and higher
nutritional value
to make it healthier for
astronauts.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
I had no idea so much thought went into
making
space food... It's really made
with the astronauts
in mind...

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text: People worked super hard to come up with these flavors...

text_block_list.name: Marvelous Sunday
text_block_list.text:
Isn't it maaarvelous when things taste

delicious? ☆★☆

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
Yeah. And this has really reminded me
taste isn't
the only thing that makes
food delicious.
